# fastf 3.18.0: todo owners, the hat, `fastf agent`, the desk and `fastf peek`

Nothing about an existing project changes. Every `PROJECT_INFO.md`,
`config.toml` and template works untouched, and no command, flag or file format
was removed. A todo nobody dates or assigns is written as it always was.

This release is for people who oversee many projects at once, with agents
working inside them. It answers three questions from the folders alone: which
todos are assigned to you, which are assigned to someone else, and which
projects have gone quiet.

## Todos carry their owner and their dates

A todo's line may end in `@owner`, `added:<stamp>` and `done:<stamp>`, each a
plain token a person or an agent can write by hand.

```markdown
- [ ] colour grade @claude added:2026-10-12T14:02:11Z
- [x] shoot @sales added:2026-09-20T10:00:00Z done:2026-09-28T18:30:00Z
```

- `fastf todo add` writes `added:`; `todo done` writes `done:` and `--undo`
  removes it; `todo edit` keeps the tokens; `todo owner <id> <n> <name>` (or
  `--none`) changes the owner; `--owner` and `--mine` on `todo add` set the
  owner as the todo is written. `todo list` shows the owner and the day.
- In the pane the owner and the day sit at the row's right, and **`O` on a
  todo** sets its owner: an owner the list already names, the hat, nobody, or
  a name you type.
- A template's starter todos may end in `@owner`, so a new project starts
  with those todos already assigned.
- `fastf journal --todos` lists every ticked todo (and with `--todos=all`,
  every added todo) between the notes, each row saying which it is; the JSON
  rows gain `kind`.
- Only the tokens at the end of the line count. A `@word` in the middle of
  the text stays text.
- A line without these tokens is a todo without an owner and without dates,
  and nothing fills them in: fastf does not know when it was written.

## The hat

`fastf hat sales` sets the hat to `@sales`. The hat is the owner name fastf
treats as yours: the app's header shows it, the desk lists the todos assigned
to it under `yours`, `todo add --mine` assigns to it, and `FASTF_HAT` sets it
for one shell without writing the config file. Nothing else reads it; the hat
never changes what a file says.

## `fastf agent`

`agent = "claude"` in `config.toml` (or `fastf config set agent claude`) names
one shell line, the shape a post-create command has. `fastf agent <query>`
runs it with the project as its working folder and `FASTF_PROJECT_PATH` set,
in the terminal you are in, so you never `cd`. From a desktop launcher it opens
a terminal window running the agent. In the app, **`x`** opens a new window
per agent so the desk stays up, and **`X`** runs it in the same terminal: the
app steps aside until the agent exits and re-reads the pane when it comes
back. fastf keeps no list of running agents: what the agent wrote in the
folder is its status.

## The desk

**`w` in the app, and `fastf desk` on the command line**: every project as
one line, grouped by who its next open todo is assigned to. The next open
todo is the first unticked todo in the file. The groups are `yours` (the
hat), `@claude`, `@acme`, `no owner` (the next todo has no `@name`) and
`no open todos`. Within a group the project nothing has written in for the
longest comes first. Each line says how long the project has been quiet,
`active` when a program is working in it right now (Linux, from the process
table), and `⚠` when the next todo is assigned to an owner, nothing has been
written in the folder for three days, and no program is working in it. No due
dates, no priorities, no lifecycle to set.

- `f` shows one group alone, `F` or Esc every group again; `s`/`S` change the
  order within a group (quiet, recent, name, id); `z` puts the cursor on a
  project picked at random. The desk's pane is the library's pane and every
  project verb works on the row under the cursor. Esc steps back to the
  library; `w` too.
- The records are read once each, a base at a time, and checked against the
  disk every ten seconds while the desk is on screen, so a todo an agent
  ticks moves its project to the right group without a keypress.
- On the command line: `fastf desk --mine`, `--owner claude`, `--no-owner`,
  `--no-open-todos`, `--quiet 7`, `--random`, `--order`, `--as <hat>`,
  `--json`. On a terminal it opens the app on the tab; `--plain` prints the
  list.
- A bare `fastf` opens on the desk when it was quit there; the session
  remembers the group, the order and when the desk was last open.

## What is going on in a project, without opening its folder

- **`fastf peek <query>`** prints one project's summary: the next open todo
  and its owner, the todo counts, which programs are working in the folder,
  the newest file under it, the repository's head (read from `.git` as files,
  no `git` started), the last note, and how long the project has been quiet.
- **The pane** gains a `glance` section ahead of the variables: `last moved`
  (the newest file under the folder, from the size scan; a dot-folder such as
  `.git` is skipped), `head`, and `working` (the programs whose working
  folder is inside the project, checked once a second while the pane shows
  it; Linux).
- **`L` gains a journal page**: every dated note and every todo added or
  ticked across every project, newest first, with a rule where the desk was
  last open, so what happened since you last looked is above the rule.

## Smaller things

- The header keeps all three tabs down to forty columns.
- `fastf show --json` carries the todos' `owner`, `added` and `done_at`.
- The settings screen has `hat` and `agent` rows beside `editor`.

Full key list: [docs/app.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/app.md);
the desk: [docs/cli.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/cli.md#the-desk).
